llm_proposer.assessment: The outage of svc275 is part of a network-wide event beginning at about t=602.5 s, localized to the common ROADM at S20. The most likely cause is a hard WSS port failure at S20, rather than either svc275 client port or one of its individual line interfaces.

proposals.rationale: Every affected working path depends on roadm.S20, while simultaneous OCH LOS, protection switching, and service failures show a common optical interruption rather than a svc275-local fault. The adjacent LOS/OSC alarms strongly localize the event to S20, although a single WSS-port failure does not by itself perfectly explain LOS indications on multiple S20 degrees.

A disconnected OMS input at S20 could produce a hard all-channel loss and the observed amplifier input LOS. It is much less likely because concurrent alarms occur on both the S20-S01 and S20-S13 directions, which would generally require more than one connection to be disturbed.

A switch-fabric failure at the common site could interrupt many ODU services simultaneously. It is strongly disfavored because it would produce ODU-layer failures without the extensive OCH, amplifier-input, and OSC LOS alarms observed here.
